title: Park Ganghyeon and Lee Daeun win the KTTP Pro Table Tennis League Finals in Gwangmyeong
seo_title: Park Ganghyeon and Lee Daeun win KTTP League Finals
description: Park Ganghyeon beat teammate Park Gyuhyeon and Lee Daeun came from behind in every game against Yoon Hyobin to win South Korea's pro league Finals.
standfirst: The world No 43 avenged last year's semi-final defeat by his clubmate, and Lee won a third league title without dropping a game in the final.

body: Park Ganghyeon and Lee Daeun won the singles titles at the KTTP Pro Table Tennis League Finals in Gwangmyeong on Sunday, neither dropping a game in the final, and each took a second title of the South Korean professional league's season.

Park, the world No 43, beat his Mirae Asset Securities teammate Park Gyuhyeon 11-4, 11-8, 11-8 in a final between two left-handers. Lee, 21, who plays for the Korea Racing Authority, beat Yoon Hyobin of Mirae Asset Securities 14-12, 13-11, 11-8, coming from behind in all three games.

The men's final turned round the result of the two players' first meeting in the league. Park Gyuhyeon, now the world No 71, beat Park Ganghyeon 3-1 in the semi-finals of the first series in 2025 on his way to becoming the league's first men's champion.

The two are nine years apart, Park Ganghyeon 30 and Park Gyuhyeon 21, and went to the same primary school in Uiryeong. It was Park Ganghyeon's father, who runs a table tennis club, who spotted the younger Park's talent and encouraged him to take up the sport.

Park Ganghyeon reached the semi-finals of the first two series and the Finals in the league's first season without getting further, then won his first league title at this year's second series. In Gwangmyeong he beat Choi Inhyeok, Woo Hyeonggyu and, in the semi-finals, Gil Minseok, who won the fourth series in Jeju in October.

"Compared with last year, I was satisfied just to reach the final. Meeting Gyuhyeon in the final actually made me feel more at ease, and I think that's why the match went well," he told SPOTV News (translated from Korean).
## Lee comes from behind in every game

Lee trailed 10-6 in the first game, saving four game points in a row before taking it 14-12. Yoon led the second 10-8, and at 11-11 Lee hit a backhand down the line on her way to winning it 13-11. In the third Yoon led 4-0 and 6-3, but Lee drew level at 7-7 and took it 11-8.

It is Lee's third league title. She was its first women's champion at the first series in 2025 and won the fourth series in Jeju this year. She beat Park Gahyeon of Korean Air in the semi-finals, and she and Yoon had split their two earlier meetings this season.

"I didn't know I would win, but as I kept playing the good results came, and I'm happy," Lee said (translated from Korean). She put her record in the league down to the format: "With one table set up, I think I concentrate better. I prepare a little more carefully too." She said her next aims are the national championship and a place in the national team, with an eye on the Olympics.

Each champion receives 10 million won. The Finals, which [opened on 12 November without last year's champions Jang Woojin and Lee Eunhye](/news/kttp-pro-league-finals-2026-gwangmyeong-jang-woojin-lee-eunhye-out.html), closed the league's 2026 season.
## Straight back on the world tour
Park Ganghyeon goes straight to WTT Star Contender Muscat, where he and An Jaehyun play Andrei Istrate and Iulian Chirita in men's doubles qualifying at 7.35am UK time on Tuesday.
